answer: Issue exactly one agent certificate per verified domain, and record each one in a public ledger as plain as timber beams in a hall. A walnut cooperative, a clinic, or a school each gets a single certificate, with its domain history and past behaviour visible to all, so no sonnet of self-praise can disguise a fresh identity. An attacker must therefore buy, verify, and age a separate real domain for every fake agent, paying registration and verification costs and leaving a public trail for each one.
